method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse paraphrase of the strong-generalization theorem and both quantified derivability clauses, stepwise replay of the two before/after tableau diagrams and two closed proof tableaux, and exact formula, macro, token, tag and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Strong generalization for tableau derivability, its eigenvariable-sensitive tableau transformation, existential introduction and universal elimination.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section states the quantified derivability facts needed for completeness. Strong generalization says that if a constant c occurs in neither Gamma nor A(x), and Gamma derives A(c), then Gamma derives universal A.
samples.checks: The nonoccurrence scope includes both Gamma and A(x), the premise remains A(c), the conclusion binds x universally, and the theorem label is exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A finite closed-tableau witness for derivability of A(c) starts with false A(c) and true B_1 through B_n from Gamma. Replace false A(c) with false universal-A and insert false A(c) after the assumptions. The old tableau continuation still closes. The inserted step is a valid false-universal application because fresh c appears nowhere above it.
samples.checks: Both schematic tableau diagrams preserve the assumption order, ellipsis, inserted node and continuation placeholders. The prose retains the exact freshness domain B_1 through B_n plus universal-A and connects it to the eigenvariable condition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The formal proposition says A(t) derives existential A and universal A derives A(t). The first closed tableau begins with false existential-A and true A(t), derives false A(t), and closes. The second begins with false A(t) and true universal-A, derives true A(t), and closes.
samples.checks: Both tagged alternatives, all signs, rule labels, line references and close markers are source-identical. The proposition block is formal-only and therefore unchanged; its two tagged proof captions are translated.

source_observations: No source correction was required in this unit.
The occurrence condition for strong generalization is verified against every formula above the inserted false-A(c) node, exactly as required by the false-universal tableau rule.
The proposition uses A(t) in sentence-level derivability claims; the displayed true-universal and false-existential applications therefore use t in the standing closed-term role from OLP-0101.
The unit contains two schematic tableau environments, two oltableau proof environments and four tagitem records in both source and target.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact Marathi terms for tableau, eigenvariable and closed term remain open to specialist review under the existing terminology ledger.
The two schematic tableau diagrams intentionally suppress line numbering and the old continuation; visual layout will be checked in the guarded chapter build.
